title: Fraud-Prevention Curricula
standfirst: Free teaching modules for AARP's Fraud Fighter Network and community organizations serving older adults. No registration, no sign-in — download and teach.

derivation.heading: Where this material comes from
derivation.body: Each module is the back of a detection model, turned around. Building a detection system requires describing a fraud scheme in exact operational terms — what the person running it has to obtain, in what order, and what traces that leaves behind. Read the other way, that same description says what the scheme looks like to the person it targets. A detection feature and a recognition cue are two renderings of one analysis: the model uses it to score an entity, and these modules use it to teach a person.

modules.title: Account Takeover and Synthetic Identity
modules.tagline: The code is not the attack. It is the alarm.
modules.summary: A 45-minute session on two schemes that both run on one piece of you: people who take over an account you already have, and people who build a new person out of your Social Security number.

modules.title: Medicare and Medicaid Billing Fraud
modules.tagline: When your Medicare number gets used without you.
modules.summary: A 45-minute session on how a Medicare or Medicaid number that seems harmless becomes a bill nobody in the room generated, the signals that appear before and after it happens, and the one thing to do about it.

facilitatorGuide.heading: The facilitator guide
facilitatorGuide.body: Each module has its own facilitator guide: a timed delivery script broken into five-to-twelve-minute segments, a 30-minute cut version for shorter slots, a specimen exercise with an answer key and the teaching reasoning behind each line, a section on the thirty seconds after a participant discloses it happened to them, room-management guidance for the ways a session tends to go sideways, and a list of things never to say and why. That is what makes a module deliverable by a volunteer who has never met the author: everything a facilitator needs to run the session is in the guide, downloaded alongside the module itself.

handoutsNote: Each module includes a one-page participant handout: plain language, large type, and a tear-off strip with the one rule and the reporting numbers to keep by the phone. The handout is what leaves the room, so it carries the action and the numbers and nothing else.
